article.title: Fal Raises $1.3 Billion Series F at $16 Billion Valuation as AI Media-Generation Demand Outpaces Its Compute Supply
article.summary: The generative-media inference startup doubled its valuation to $16 billion after demand for its image, video and audio models forced it to rate-limit customers.
article.body_markdown:
## Overview

Fal, a San Francisco startup that runs AI image, video and audio generation models for developers, has raised $1.3 billion in a Series F round led by Bessemer Venture Partners, valuing the company at $16 billion, double the $8 billion valuation it held in April, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/) and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ai-inference-startup-fal-doubles-its-valuation-to-16b-as-demand-surges/). Both outlets, citing Bloomberg, reported the deal on November 3.

Fal disclosed the Series F alongside an earlier, previously unannounced Series E: a $350 million round led by Sequoia Capital in April that closed at the same $8 billion valuation, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/). Fal said the two rounds together total $1.65 billion, a figure confirmed independently by [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ai-inference-startup-fal-doubles-its-valuation-to-16b-as-demand-surges/).

## What We Know

Fal provides a cloud platform for running image, video and audio generation models, with developers reaching all of them through a single API, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/). Entertainment studios, advertising agencies and game developers are among the customers using those models in production, the company told the outlet. In-house researchers also post-train some models to run faster, work that has centered on video over the past year, done in partnership with the model developers; some of those deals pay fal licensing fees or a share of revenue, per [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/).

Co-founder and Chief Executive Burkay Gur told Bloomberg the round is as large as it is because demand surged faster than fal's compute capacity. "We hit a point in summer where we were not able to serve our customers and had to rate-limit them," he said, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/). Pretraining a model of fal's own is not on the near-term agenda, Gur said, though he did not rule it out for later.

Annualized revenue at fal passed $800 million earlier this year, a person familiar with the matter told Bloomberg, a figure both [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/) and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ai-inference-startup-fal-doubles-its-valuation-to-16b-as-demand-surges/) reported. The company plans to spend the new capital on computing power and on hiring beyond its current 185 employees, per [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/).

Gur started the company in 2021 with Chief Technology Officer Gorkem Yurtseven. Gur previously led machine learning work at Coinbase Global Inc. and held an engineering role at Oracle Corp.; Yurtseven was previously a developer at Amazon.com Inc., according to both [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/) and [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ai-inference-startup-fal-doubles-its-valuation-to-16b-as-demand-surges/).

Bessemer Venture Partners led the Series F, and its partner Talia Goldberg is joining the board of Features & Labels Inc., as fal is formally known, [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/) reported. Nvidia Corp., Sound Ventures, HOF Capital and T. Rowe Price Group Inc. also participated; fal described Nvidia as a strategic investor, per the same report. Last December, the company had raised $140 million at a $4.5 billion valuation, SiliconANGLE reported, putting total investment in fal at more than $1.9 billion to date.

## Industry Context

The raise puts fal just behind rival inference provider Fireworks AI Inc., which closed $1.5 billion in funding at a $17.5 billion valuation in July, according to [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/11/03/generative-media-inference-startup-fal-raises-1-3b-at-a-16b-valuation/). [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/ai-inference-startup-fal-doubles-its-valuation-to-16b-as-demand-surges/) named Baseten, Fireworks AI and Modal as other inference providers that have also been growing quickly and raising large rounds at higher valuations, but reported that gross margins across the sector remain thin because of the high cost of buying or leasing the compute needed to run the models. Modal Labs itself [previously raised](/article/2026-05/25-modal-labs-closes-355-million-series-c-at-465-billion-as-serverless-ai-cloud-quadruples-revenue) a $355 million Series C at a $4.65 billion valuation in May.

## What We Don't Know

Neither SiliconANGLE nor TechCrunch disclosed how much of the $1.3 billion fal plans to allocate specifically to new compute purchases versus hiring, or what fal's current gross margin looks like. Fal did not itself publish the $800 million revenue figure; it was attributed by both outlets to a person familiar with the matter speaking to Bloomberg, rather than to a company disclosure.
